newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CARLING CRITICAL OF ENGLAND TEAM-MATES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CARLING CRITICAL OF ENGLAND TEAM-MATES.

text.p: Former England captain Will Carling has entered the row over the future of English rugby by criticising his international colleagues for supporting a breakaway from the Rugby Football Union (RFU).

Carling disagrees with the decision of the country's top players to side with EPRUC, the body representing the senior English clubs in a bitter power struggle with Twickenham, which could cost them their places in the official national team.
"I wouldn't have signed for EPRUC because I don't think they're really offering an awful lot," said Carling, who quit the captaincy in March.
"It's a very hard position to put the players in and it's not one I would have allowed myself to have been put in. I don't think the players should take sides.
"I want to play for England and I don't think it's right that anyone asks you not to play for your country.
"To play for country is an incredible honour. I don't think anyone should ever ask you to put that in jeopardy."
Carling was not among the 40-plus group of players who boycotted a training session earlier this month, but could be drafted back into the squad for a scheduled training session on Wednesday week.
